{{Quote|In many ways, some have described it as a surrender to the Force and to chaos, to strike at an opponent with such speed and angles of attack that they have difficulty countering it. ''[&hellip;]'' But in surrendering yourself to the Force in such a way reduces your ability to resist its effects should the enemy turn the Force against you. Be on your guard.|Kreia teaches Meetra Surik|<ref name="TSL">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
'''Form VII''', also known as '''Juyo''' in [[High Galactic (language)|High Galactic]]<ref name="saga4">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050526a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 4: Of the Crudest Matter}}</ref>, '''the Way of the [[Vornskr]]''', or '''the Ferocity Form''', was the seventh of seven forms recognized as canon for [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] by the last [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Old Jedi Order]]. In use, millennia before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Juyo incarnation of Form VII was described as the most vicious form of [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] combat and was said to involve a significant internal focus on the part of the user. Juyo had many practitioners throughout the years, including [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Kavar]], [[Zez-Kai Ell]], and [[Vrook Lamar]]. Due to its relatively high focus on one's internal emotions to gain dominance in combat, Form VII oscillated from simply being looked down upon to outright being seen as a taboo. Knowledge of Form VII became restricted among the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Order, whose members were worried that its precepts would lead practitioners toward the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. In contrast, members of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], such as [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], employed Juyo without reservation, as did [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] such as [[Galen Marek]].

In the later days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], a new variation of Form VII, dubbed '''Vaapad''' after a [[Vaapad/Legends|creature]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sarapin/Legends|Sarapin]], was created by Jedi Masters [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] and [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]]. Vaapad was explained as being a state of mind rather than just a fighting style, allowing the wielder to channel their inner darkness into the duel and accept the opponent's fury. Windu, Bulq, Windu's former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Depa Billaba/Legends|Depa Billaba]], and [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] were four notable practitioners of the Vaapad variant. Records of both Juyo and Vaapad survived the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] and were recovered by the [[New Jedi Order]], who preserved the records of Form VII into the [[Sith–Imperial War]].

==Description==
[[File:Vaapad - SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|250px|right|A Vaapad practitioner]]
{{Quote|I created Vaapad to answer my weakness: it channels my own darkness into a weapon of the light.|Mace Windu to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="ROTSnovel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Revenge of the Sith novelization'']]</ref>}}
There were two variations of Form VII, Juyo and Vaapad, but both utilized bold, direct movements. According to accounts compiled by the [[New Jedi Order]], the use of Form VII was more demanding in terms of energy used due to a broader focus and deeper utilization of emotion. A Form VII practitioner was said to maintain a calm exterior appearance. Still, they were also stated to experience significant internal pressure while using the Ferocity Form.<ref name="EGTTF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> In addition, it was described as sometimes paradoxical and unpredictable and filled with concepts that made the form too difficult and unattractive to many students.<ref name="Hero's Guide">''[[Hero's Guide]]''</ref>

===Juyo===
{{Quote|Predictably, he seeks to unbalance you with his erratic attacks. His technique is called Juyo, the most chaotic of the lightsaber forms. This form sacrifices much to bolster the offense, leaving one exposed to attack by the Force.|Kreia to the Jedi Exile|<ref name="TSL" />}}
[[File:SWEP1TPM4-FC.jpg|thumb|left|160px|[[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], a Juyo practitioner, used the form against [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].]]
Juyo was described as the most vicious form of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] and was said to be filled with both fury and "malignant grace."<ref name="TFU">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> The form was given the title of the most difficult and demanding form in all of the lightsaber combat.<ref name="EGTTF" /> Skilled combatants with Juyo were said by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vrook Lamar]] to be able to "eviscerate a lone enemy";<ref name="TSL" /> in fact, it was designed for such a purpose in one-on-one lightsaber duels.<ref name="TOR:A">''[[The Old Republic: Annihilation]]''</ref> According to the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Kreia|Darth Traya]], the form was both chaotic and erratic, with a heavy focus on offense,<ref name="TSL" /> and using techniques believed to have been rejected from Shii-Cho in the earliest days of the Jedi Order.<ref name="Knights">''[[Knights of Fate]]''</ref> Juyo's use was controversial among the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], as many felt that Juyo violated the "there is no emotion, there is peace" tenet of the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]] due to its requirement to fight under the guidance of controlled passion. The Sith had no such inhibition, and [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] went so far as to label it a "Sith style."<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

[[Battlemaster/Legends|Jedi Battlemaster]] [[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]] listed bold, direct motions as characteristics of Juyo, qualifying them as more open and kinetic than [[Form V/Legends|Form V]], but with a less elaborate appearance than [[Form IV/Legends|Ataru]]. Drallig contrasted the tactics of Juyo as not nearly as graceful or linked as those of Ataru, instead referring to them as "seemingly unconnected staccato sequences." He also listed one of the strengths of the form as its unpredictability. The form was said to necessitate greater energy than Form V due to a broader wielding of a user's focus and a deeper emotional link. Despite the challenges inherent in using the form, it could serve as a pathway to considerable power.<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber">{{SWArchive|url=games/videogames/news20080728.html|text=Fightsaber: Mastering the Art of Lightsaber Combat}}</ref>

===Vaapad===
{{Quote|This is called Vaapad, Kar. How many arms do you see?|Mace Windu facing Kar Vastor in unarmed combat|<ref name="shatterpoint" />}}
Vaapad was described as more than a fighting style; it was a state of mind that led through the penumbra of the dark side, requiring the user to enjoy the fight and relish the satisfaction of winning. The practitioner of Vaapad would accept the fury of their opponent, transforming themselves into one half of a superconducting loop, with the other half being the power of darkness inherent in the opponent.<ref name="EGTTF" /> The form was also mentioned with a cautionary warning by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] that the use of Vaapad led the user perilously close to the dark side due to its focus on physical combat.<ref name="Fightsaber" /> Vaapad required a constant and sizable stream of Force use from the user, with a barely contained explosion of Force power essential to all variations of Form VII as another prerequisite for its use. The form's attacks appeared to be unconnected, its motions seemingly unpolished to an untrained observer.<ref name="Fact File">{{FactFile|112|LIG 19-20|Mace Windu's Lightsabers}}</ref>

[[File:WinduvsBulq.jpg|thumb|right|260px|[[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] and [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]], the two creators of Vaapad, [[Mission to Ruul (Clone Wars)|duel]] each other on [[Ruul (moon)|Ruul]].]]
During the later years of the Republic, Jedi Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] developed Vaapad with the aid of fellow master [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]], by drawing inspiration from the movements of a [[Vaapad/Legends|creature]],<ref name="shatterpoint" /> known as both the Vaapad and the Juyo,<ref name="SWI92">[[Star Wars Insider 92|''Star Wars Insider'' 92]]</ref> native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sarapin/Legends|Sarapin]]. Vaapad users appeared to wield many [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] at once, moving too fast to see, just as the vaapad creature would attack with blindingly fast tentacles that were impossible to count until the vaapad was [[Death/Legends|dead]]. A Vaapad user's attacks would flow into each other with liquid precision, creating the constant near-invisible weave of energy which was the ready-stance of Vaapad. It was also possible to apply Vaapad in unarmed combat, with the user's arms becoming too fast to see, as well as in the use of [[Jar'Kai/Legends|dual]] lightsabers.<ref name="shatterpoint" /> While observing the duel between [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] and Mace Windu, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] considered Windu's Vaapad bladework to be "an oblate sphere of purple fire" which contained dozens of blades attacking from every angle.<ref name="ROTSnovel" />

After his fall to the dark side before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] described the power of Vaapad as skirting the dark side of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], but stated during a duel with Sora Bulq that the form was bridled and weak without direct use of the dark side. Dooku later subverted Bulq to his cause.<ref name="Trackdown">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Trackdown]]''</ref> After Bulq fell to the dark side, he claimed that he had perfected the form, which Windu disputed while [[Mission to Ruul (Clone Wars)|engaging]] Bulq in a lightsaber duel. While Bulq had previously practiced Vaapad with Windu, he was unable to defeat him in combat and their duel ended in a stalemate.<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" /> Though Windu and Bulq were credited with the creation of the Vaapad variant, the seventh lightsaber form was known, albeit obscurely, by the name Vaapad as early as the end of the [[New Sith Wars]] by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith Blademaster|Blademaster]] [[Kas'im]].<ref name="BOS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

==Applications==
{{Quote|Vaapad is more than a fighting style. It is a state of mind, a path that leads through the penumbra of the dark side.|Mace Windu|<ref name="EGTTF" />}}
[[File:Depalightsaber.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Mace Windu's former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Depa Billaba/Legends|Depa Billaba]], was skilled in the use of Vaapad.]]
Millennia prior to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Juyo was ascribed the moniker of the "Ferocity form" due to its aggressive nature. Jedi Master [[Zez-Kai Ell]] claimed that Juyo was highly effective against an armed opponent, though much less against a foe skilled with the use of the Force. Master [[Kavar]], a colleague of Zez-Kai Ell, advised Juyo for use in quickly overwhelming a single foe as well but cautioned that it left one vulnerable to Force attacks such as those employed by [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]]. Jedi of this era prescribed caution and control when using Juyo and were reluctant to teach it to those with known recklessness, as the form's ferocity could lead them to the dark side.<ref name="TSL" /> Juyo was said to be able to destroy even the defenses of a [[Form III/Legends|Form III]] master, but the practitioner was left vulnerable to counter-attack in the process, particularly from multiple opponents and Force powers.<ref name="TJP" />

According to Jedi battlemaster Cin Drallig, who served in the final days of the Old Republic, Form VII was sufficiently demanding that only masters skilled in practicing multiple other forms were capable of utilizing it effectively. Drallig stated that the mastery required to learn Form VII was such that only a select few would be allowed to utilize it; he forbade its study to all others. At least two users of its Vaapad variant during Drallig's tenure described the form as dangerous due to its focus on physical combat and intensity.<ref name="EGTTF" /> For his part, [[Cin Drallig/Legends|Drallig]] refused to allow [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] to study Juyo. At the same time [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was likewise forbidden to learn Vaapad by [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]].<ref name="TJP" /> Windu also discouraged [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] from learning Vaapad when Vos used it in a practice duel, learning from Vos that he had learned the move from Bulq and warning him against using it again, due to Vos already being perilously close to the dark side.<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" />

Jedi Master Mace Windu, who developed Vaapad along with Weequay Jedi Sora Bulq,<ref name="EGTTF" /> stated that Vaapad was an answer for his own weakness, allowing him to channel his own internal darkness into something positive.<ref name="ROTSnovel" /> Furthermore, he said that he would not allow the use of the form without his permission, something that he had only given to his apprentice, [[Depa Billaba/Legends|Depa Billaba]].<ref name="EGTTF" /> Jedi Master [[Siri Tachi/Legends|Siri Tachi]] once explained to her [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Ferus Olin]], that the reason Mace Windu was able to dismiss the pleasure in power which Vaapad brought was by acknowledging it and being constantly aware of it.<ref name="RotDS">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Return of the Dark Side]]''</ref> Windu wielded the form in numerous battles,<ref name="Fightsaber" /><ref name="shatterpoint" /><ref name="EGTTF" /> especially in the [[Petranaki arena]] [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|against]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], where his relentless use of Vaapad overpowered Fett.<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber" />

While [[Showdown on Coruscant|dueling]] Darth Sidious in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], The Sith Lord quickly brought down mace Windu's three Jedi companions. To combat Sidious' furious technique, Windu gave himself entirely over to Vaapad. He allowed it to fully channel his inner darkness and accept and use Sidious's darkness. When fully immersed in his form, Windu's fighting prowess was such that he could allow his body to fight automatically for him without needing to direct it with his mind. Sidious' own fury was used and redirected by Windu via the use of Vaapad, a process which Windu mentally likened to a lightsaber deflecting a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolt back at its source.<ref name="ROTSnovel" /> After Windu disarmed Sidious, the Sith Lord attempted to blast him with [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]],<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> but Windu responded by once more employing Vaapad techniques to channel the dark power of the lightning through him without it affecting him; he then redirected it back to its source. However, Windu believed that his use of Vaapad alone was insufficient to defeat Sidious, as he felt it would only result in a stalemate.<ref name="ROTSnovel" />

==Known moves and maneuvers==
{{Quote|That last move&hellip; It was a Form VII maneuver. Vaapad.|Mace Windu, to Quinlan Vos|<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu">''[[Jedi: Mace Windu]]''</ref>}}
[[File:WinduVosVaapad.jpg|thumb|right|225px|Quinlan Vos applying a Vaapad maneuver against Mace Windu.]]
It should be noted that while the sequences and maneuvers of Form VII could be practiced and drilled, a duelist would not be truly executing the style unless they allowed the excitement and passion of battle to color their actions.<ref name="TJP" /> The Form VII opening stance was a one-handed high guard with the blade held horizontally above the head and pointed to the side. The body was half-twisted, with the off-hand swept across and down.<ref name="MysteriesOfTheJedi">''[[Star Wars: Mysteries of the Jedi]]''</ref> Juyo users were proficient in a technique called "Assured Strike," wherein they traded sheer power for a near-certainty of landing a hit. Another technique they used was referred to as "Vornskr's Ferocity," which involved "ferocious" attacking of an opponent. Wielders of Juyo were capable of employing this move without allowing the dark side's influence to pervade their aggression.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref>

Those skilled in the Vaapad form were known for their use of the "Swift Flank" technique, where they leaped or dashed around an opponent to make a quick strike. The speed of the maneuver was intended to catch opponents off guard. They were also skilled in "Tempered Aggression," a term used to describe the ferocity of the Vaapad form, but with more control against succumbing to the dark side even in the heat of battle.<ref name="JATM" />

==Practitioners==
===Juyo===
{{Quote|I accept only a handful of students - handpicked according to my personal standards - each year. Never again will I permit the widespread use of this form after the events of the last Sith War, when ''Juyo'' provided the trigger for Jedi to sink into butchery and join the ranks of the Sith.|[[Skarch Vaunk]] in [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]|<ref name="TJP" />}}
[[File:Juyo_Ataru.png|thumb|left|250px|Darth Maul utilizing Juyo against Obi-Wan Kenobi's usage of Ataru.]]
Juyo was an established form of combat four millennia prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Jedi Masters Vrook Lamar, Zez-Kai Ell, and Kavar were all skilled in its use and were able to pass on their experience to others.<ref name="TSL" /> Jedi Master [[Atris]], who fell to the dark side during the [[First Jedi Purge]], was also known to employ the form.<ref name="KotORCG" /> [[Jaric Kaedan]], a Jedi Master who fought in the [[Great Galactic War]], was a master of the form&mdash;which was known as Juyo-Kos by that time&mdash;and he was considered a living weapon guided by the will of the Force itself.<ref name="LS1">[[The Old Republic — The Lost Suns 1|''The Old Republic — The Lost Suns'' 1]]</ref> Other Great Galactic War combatants, Jedi Master Gnost-Dural and the Sith Lord [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]], also employed Juyo.<ref name="TOR:A" /><ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic: Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref> 

The Sith Blademaster Kas'im was a master of all seven forms of lightsaber combat near the end of the New Sith Wars, and the Sith apprentice [[Sirak]], who was stationed on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] during Kas'im's tenure there, was known to incorporate Juyo thrusts and jabs into his fighting style.<ref name="PoD" /> Another Sith Lord of that era, [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], was proficient in the use of Juyo.<ref name="TotG">''[[Threats of the Galaxy]]''</ref> During the New Sith Wars, the use of Juyo caused many Jedi to fall to the dark side and join forces with the Sith. As a result, the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] restricted the use of the Form, and in the time following the end of the conflict, the Jedi battlemaster [[Skarch Vaunk]] trained Juyo to only a few hand-picked students each year.<ref name="TJP" />

[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] had achieved mastery of Juyo, and his competence was great enough to train [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] in its use. Maul's inner aggression complimented his use of the form and he used it as his primary method of lightsaber combat, drawing heavily on the dark side to gain the ability to overwhelm opponents through sheer ferocity. His most notable usage was during [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], when [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|battling]] Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and Jedi Padawan [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], Maul showed the ability to adapt Juyo into the use of a [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]]. Maul's use of the form was enough for him to fight both highly skilled Jedi at once despite Juyo's weakness to multiple foes. When he engaged them one-on-one, Maul quickly broke through Qui-Gon Jinn's defenses, allowing him to slay the Jedi Master.<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber" /> However, Maul was devoted to the physical aspect of Form VII, as the Sith sought a purely physical victory over any enemy no matter how numerous,<ref name="Fightsaber" /> but by the Clone Wars, Maul grew out of this, now incorporating the Force. He was able to fully master Juyo.<ref name="UK Comic 6.35">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.35|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.35]]</ref> His skills could overwhelm the defenses of even Kenobi, one of the greatest masters of Soresu. In fact, Form VII had fewer practitioners than other styles, due to its difficulty, complexity, and demands.<ref name="Hero's Guide" />

[[File:Kota_vs_Starkiller1.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Both [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]] and [[Galen Marek]] heavily favored Juyo.]]
Jedi Battlemaster Cin Drallig and Grand Master Yoda had knowledge and mastery of all seven forms, including Juyo, befitting Drallig's role as lightsaber combat instructor at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] and Yoda's reputation of having mastered all forms of lightsaber combat<ref name="EGTTF" /> as did [[Anoon Bondara]], another lightsaber instructor.<ref name="JATM" /> [[Lannik (species)/Legends|Lannik]] Jedi Master [[Even Piell/Legends|Even Piell]] was familiar with all seven forms of lightsaber combat, including Form VII.<ref name="Jedi Twilight">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref> Furthermore, his Padawan, [[Jax Pavan]], had some knowledge of the Juyo form, which he learned during his time in the Jedi Order.<ref name="Patterns of Force">''[[Coruscant Nights III: Patterns of Force]]''</ref> Another practitioner of Juyo was the grizzled [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], who survived both [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] and the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]].<ref name="TFUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Mace Windu and Sora Bulq, who co-created the Vaapad variant of Form VII, were particularly skilled and knowledgeable in the use of Juyo, enough to together perfect the form into Vaapad.<ref name="CWCG">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

Darth Vader's secret apprentice, [[Galen Marek]], was proficient in the use of Juyo, with his concentration and aggression being enough to bring down opponents with sheer tenacity. His application of Juyo was also laced with sudden Force-based attacks in the midst of complex lightsaber sequences, making him highly unpredictable. Marek used the form against both a vision of himself while on the planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] and against the fallen Jedi [[Maris Brood]] on [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]] in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]]. Marek's [[Droid/Legends|droid]] companion, [[PROXY]] could use an imitation of the form, albeit without the Force, which he fought with while dueling Marek in the guise of Anakin Skywalker.<ref name="TFU" /> After his defeat in the [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|Duel on Mustafar]], Vader himself studied Form VII and became a master of it, at times applying elements of Juyo as part of his customized variant of Form V,<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber" /> employing some of its techniques when he killed the resistance fighter, [[Roan Lands]], who was a good friend of the former Jedi Ferus Olin.<ref name="SW">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Secret Weapon]]''</ref> Knowledge of Juyo in the book ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]'' and records compiled by Jedi Master Cin Drallig was passed on to the [[New Jedi Order]] after the [[Great Holocron/Legends|Great Holocron]] was recovered. The New Jedi Order then preserved this information into the [[Sith–Imperial War]].<ref name="TJP" /><ref name="EGTTF" />

The [[Majestrix of Skye|Majestrix]] [[Kharys]] of [[Skye]], adapted Juyo, mixing it with traditional [[S'kytri]] aerial techniques, to create the rare variant known as [[Trispzest]].<ref name="saga4" />

===Vaapad===
{{Quote|Form seven is very ''aggressive,'' Quin. It can take the user very close to the dark side&mdash;and ''you,'' frankly, sometimes walk too close there as it is.|Mace Windu|<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" />}}
[[File:Swirling_VZZZ.jpg|200px|thumb|left|Mace Windu was known among the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] for his use of Vaapad, a variation of Form VII.]]
Weequay Jedi Master Sora Bulq, already considered one of the Jedi Order's finest lightsaber practitioners and skilled in all seven forms,<ref name="Sora Bulq Databank">{{DB|character|sorabulq|Bulq, Sora}}</ref> helped Mace Windu perfect Vaapad in the later years of the Republic. After the Battle of Geonosis, Bulq became disillusioned with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the Jedi Order and fell to the dark side.<ref name="GatORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> As was later said by Windu, Bulq did not master Vaapad; Vaapad mastered him.<ref name="Sora Bulq Databank" />

Before falling, Bulq also taught Quinlan Vos some maneuvers from Vaapad when the amnesiac [[Kiffar/Legends|Kiffar]] needed retraining. Vos would later demonstrate his new talents inadvertently during a practice session with Mace Windu, who immediately recognized his move as part of Vaapad. Windu abruptly halted the duel, warning Vos not to use Vaapad again, as Vos was already considered to tread too closely to the dark side for him to safely employ Vaapad.<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" /> However, while Vos was serving as a double agent for Count Dooku during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], he was encouraged by Bulq, who had by that time allied with Dooku, to take up Vaapad's power again.<ref name="Jedi: Count Dooku">''[[Jedi: Count Dooku]]''</ref> Mace Windu, in his private memoir, expressed concerns and suspected Vos had mastered Vaapad to a degree greater than the Kiffar revealed.<ref name="EGTTF" /> During the [[Siege of Saleucami/Legends|Siege of Saleucami]], Dooku, Bulq and [[Tol Skorr]] prodded Quinlan Vos to give himself over to the dark side and to Vaapad; Vos thereby demonstrated his level of mastery of Vaapad in his duels with Skorr and Bulq, defeating both in lightsaber combat and completing his mastery of the flow of light and dark mastery of Vaapad requires as exemplified when Vos was freed from Bulq's [[Mind trick/Legends#Force illusion|Force illusions]].<ref name="Siege of Saleucami">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Siege of Saleucami]]''</ref>

[[File:Vaapad_windu.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Mace Windu using the Vaapad form in combat.]]
The only student Mace Windu ever taught Vaapad to was his Padawan, Depa Billaba. Under Windu's instruction, Billaba became a master of Vaapad, with Windu considering her virtually unbeatable in personal combat. While on a mission with her master to [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], Billaba and Windu were forced into a deadly confrontation with a mutated giant [[Akk dog/Legends|akks]]. They barely survived the encounter, and Windu would later comment that on that day, Billaba had shown blade work that surpassed his own. While on a mission to [[Haruun Kal/Legends|Haruun Kal]], Billaba fell to the dark side, allowing the blood fever of the jungle and the pull of Vaapad to take over. Mace Windu was forced to [[Battle of Haruun Kal/Legends|travel]] to Haruun Kal and face his student in a duel. Windu discovered that the only way he could survive against his former Padawan was to give all of himself to Vaapad, but realized that if he did, he would fall to the dark side as well. Turning away from the dark side, Windu conceded the fight, purposely opening himself up for Billaba's killing strike. However, Billaba, seeing what she had become, attempted to take her own life but was stopped by timely [[Nick Rostu|outside intervention]].<ref name="shatterpoint" />

While fighting the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], Windu again displayed his mastery of Vaapad. Grievous responded by mimicking Windu's style, which resulted in what Windu considered a passable imitation of the form. Grievous had instructed his personal [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuard]] droids in all seven forms of lightsaber combat, including Form VII.<ref name="Labyrinth of Evil">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> As with Juyo, knowledge of Form VII was recovered from ''The Jedi Path'' and the Great Holocron by the New Jedi Order, who preserved the information into the Sith-Imperial War.<ref name="TJP" /><ref name="EGTTF" />

==Behind the scenes==
Form VII was first mentioned as part of the ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''. However, little information was given about its characteristics or users, except that Jedi Master Mace Windu employed it. Along with the other six classical saber forms, it was heavily described by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]] and fencer Jack "Stelen" Bobo for the "''[[Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat]]''" part of [[Star Wars Insider 62|''Star Wars Insider'' 62]]. This same source also [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]]ed Darth Maul's use of Form VII in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']],<ref name="Fightsaber" /> while a [[StarWars.com]] web page derived from the ''Fightsaber'' piece later established that Mace Windu had wielded Vaapad against Jango Fett in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber" /> Windu's Vaapad-inspired fighting style was to be first mentioned in the reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Episode I]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and was later revealed in other sources after that book's cancellation.<ref name="EpI EG">{{Blog|danwallace|34|Lostwords: The Essential Guide to Episode I}}</ref>

Form VII was then expounded upon in numerous other sources, including ''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', and numerous supplementary works and [[Roleplaying game|RPG]] guides, which expanded its list of practitioners and established Juyo as a known form circa the [[Jedi Civil War]].<ref name="TSL" /><ref name="PoD" /> The Clone Wars novel [[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']] had a large focus and considerable description on the Vaapad variant, as two of the principal characters, Mace Windu and Depa Billaba, were masters of the form.<ref name="shatterpoint" /> Several issues of comics set during the Clone Wars, including [[Star Wars: Republic: Trackdown|''Trackdown'']] from the ''[[Star Wars: Republic]]'' story arc, as well as ''[[Jedi: Mace Windu]]'' and ''[[Jedi: Count Dooku]]'', featured Vaapad in a substantial role, due to the involvement of Mace Windu and Sora Bulq.<ref name="Trackdown" /><ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" /><ref name="Jedi: Count Dooku" />

Both Juyo and Vaapad were extensively described in the [[2007]] reference book [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']], which provided an entry for Form VII, as well as a longer description of Vaapad. ''The Essential Guide to the Force'' established that knowledge of the seven forms, including Juyo and Vaapad, survived into the [[Legacy era]].<ref name="EGTTF" />

In the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords'', the Jedi Masters could teach the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] the Juyo form only if she was [[Jedi Guardian/Legends|Jedi Guardian]] or its corresponding prestige classes, the [[Jedi Weapon Master]] or the [[Sith Marauder]].<ref name="TSL" />

The Sith apprentice [[Sirak]] in ''Darth Bane: Path of Destruction'' was a Vaapad practitioner long before Mace Windu created the style.<ref name="PoD" /> At a book signing in Huntington Beach, California, author [[Drew Karpyshyn]] said, "I meant Juyo, but it was a late night when I wrote that and didn't catch it until it was too late. That's one mistake I wish to God I could change. So when you read it and see 'Vaapad,' just pretend it says 'Juyo.'"<ref name="KarpyBlog">{{Blog|DrewK|2|Why I ruined everything for everyone: Continuity in Path of Destruction}}</ref> [[Star Wars Insider 92|''Star Wars Insider'' 92]] later explained it by stating that "juyo" was another term for the [[Vaapad/Legends|vaapad]] creature the form was named after.<ref name="SWI92" />

Form VII, along with the other lightsaber forms, appears in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' as part of moves and techniques employable by Jedi characters. This has not definitively been clarified to be [[canon]]ical.<ref name="SonyCite-Jedi Abilities: Learning the Way">{{SonyCite|url=en_US/players/content.vm?id=66843&resource=features|text=Jedi Abilities: Learning the Way}}</ref>

In ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', Juyo is the form of choice for the Watchman specialization available to Jedi Sentinels, as well as the Annihilation specialization available to Sith Marauders. Both of those specializations utilize an aggressive, acrobatic style of combat focused on inflicting damage over time. The form itself is only a passive ability and does not cause any visual changes in the fighting style.

Form VII is displayed as part of the non-canonical guest appearance of Darth Vader in the fighting game ''[[Soulcalibur IV]]'' as part of Vader's repertoire of moves.<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber" /><ref name="Soul Calibur IV">''[[Soulcalibur IV]]''</ref>

In the non-canonical bossfight between [[Kyle Katarn]] and [[Jaden Korr]] in [[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]], Kyle seems proficient in Vapaad .
